title: Underwriting Rule on One Larkspur Personal Umbrella Policy per Household
content:
**Rule.** A household carries one Larkspur Personal Umbrella. The customer holds no other umbrella that is bound, in force or pending cancellation. A higher limit is obtained by rewriting the existing umbrella at renewal, never by stacking a second one.

The most Larkspur Personal Umbrella Policy contracts a customer may hold at once in those statuses is 1.

## Basis of the judgement

Whether a new Larkspur Personal Umbrella Policy may be bound for a customer is judged on the company's own umbrella records for that customer, as they stand before the new umbrella is bound. What decides it is the status of each umbrella already on record under the same customer.

| Status of an umbrella already on record for the customer | Does it stand in the way of binding another? |
|---|---|
| Bound | Yes |
| In force | Yes |
| Pending cancellation | Yes |
| Cancelled | No |
| Expired | No |

An umbrella in any of the first three statuses counts as held; an umbrella that has been cancelled or has expired does not.

## Points of judgement

- **A larger limit.** The one-umbrella rule does not bar a higher limit; it fixes the way to it. A household that wants a higher limit has its existing umbrella rewritten at renewal to the higher tier. A second umbrella stacked over or beside the first is never bound.
- **Hypothetical:** a customer whose only umbrella on record expired at the end of its last term holds no umbrella in a counting status, so the rule does not stand in the way of a new one.
- **Hypothetical:** a customer whose umbrella is pending cancellation still holds that umbrella for this rule, and a second umbrella is not bound while it remains in that status.
